cards.meaning: Boot/hardware/driver → dmesg; unit/service since systemd → journalctl; classic syslog files → /var/log/…
cards.notes: Three places Linux records what kernel, services, and daemons did

cards.meaning: Prints the kernel message ring buffer
cards.notes: Filled from early boot and later kernel events (disk errors, OOM, USB, NIC). Not the same as /var/log/messages

cards.meaning: Kernel's own size-limited message buffer; old lines fall off
cards.notes: First place for "did the kernel even see this device?"

cards.meaning: Kernel messages with human-readable (wall-clock) timestamps
cards.notes: Instead of seconds since boot. Kernel diary with wall-clock times

cards.meaning: Disk/NIC/USB missing, kernel panic, boot command line, RAM e820 map
cards.example: look for Command line, e820 usable vs reserved
cards.notes: Version, root device, LVM, crashkernel show up early in the buffer

cards.meaning: System service that collects and stores logging data into structured, indexed binary journals
cards.notes: Centralizes logs from kernel, unit stdout/stderr, syslog, audit, and more

cards.meaning: Query and display systemd journal data
cards.notes: Journals are binary (not tailable as plain text) — always go through journalctl

cards.meaning: Follow the journal (live tail of new entries)
cards.notes: Mentioned as the follow form of journalctl

cards.meaning: Journal lines for that systemd unit only (e.g. Apache)
cards.notes: -u = unit/service filter

cards.meaning: Priority error and worse; this boot only; add explanatory help texts when available
cards.notes: Combined filter from the course

cards.meaning: Filter by priority / log level (e.g. err = error and worse: crit, alert, emerg)
cards.notes: Also warning, info, debug, …

cards.meaning: Only entries since last boot (this boot)
cards.notes: -b -1 is previous boot

cards.meaning: Add explanatory help texts where available (context, possible solutions, docs links)
cards.notes: Short help explaining the log event

cards.meaning: Only entries for syslog identifier dockerd
cards.notes: Identifier is not necessarily the unit name (-u docker.service). Same process can show as unit and syslog id

cards.meaning: Show messages from a start time (relative or absolute)
cards.notes: Also "2 days ago" or an absolute timestamp. Combine with -u, -p, -t

cards.meaning: Show messages until an end time (with --since for a window)
cards.notes: Time box for journal queries

cards.meaning: -u unit · -t syslog name · -p level · -b this boot · -x extra help · --since / --until time box
cards.notes: Recall sheet for journalctl filters

cards.meaning: Global system messages including startup; mail, cron, daemon, kern, auth, etc.
cards.notes: On Debian/Ubuntu the closest general file is often /var/log/syslog instead

cards.meaning: Authentication and authorization; sshd including unsuccessful logins (RHEL-family)
cards.notes: Who tried to log in on RHEL-style systems

cards.meaning: Cron / anacron job starts and related cron daemon info
cards.notes: Scheduled jobs

cards.meaning: System authorization: user logins and authentication mechanisms used
cards.notes: Typical on Debian-family; RHEL uses /var/log/secure for much of the same story

cards.meaning: Mail server log (e.g. sendmail sent items)
cards.notes: RHEL-style mail log name

cards.meaning: Mail server log — Debian-style name for the same idea
cards.notes: Same role as maillog, different distro naming

cards.meaning: Subdirectory with additional mail-server logs
cards.notes: Extra mail logs beyond maillog / mail.log

cards.meaning: Daily sar files collected by the sysstat package
cards.notes: sar (CPU / storage topics) reads this history

cards.meaning: On many distros still write classic text logs under /var/log besides the journal
cards.notes: Journal is the systemd-era query tool on top of (or instead of) these files

cards.meaning: messages = general; secure / auth.log = who tried to log in; cron = scheduled jobs; sa/ = sar history
cards.notes: Classic path cheat sheet
